meta.title: loadcli — your entire dev environment, in one click
meta.description: One click creates a fresh desktop on the right monitor, opens the Terminal with your CLI already in the project folder and tiles the browser beside it. Native macOS app, open source, and SIP stays on.

hero.title:
Your entire dev
environment, in
one click.
hero.lead: Pick a project. loadcli spins up a fresh desktop on the monitor you want, opens the Terminal with your CLI already in the project folder, and tiles the browser beside it. Everything placed, focus on the terminal.
aside: Each project's card is a LOADCLI.md inside its own folder. Sync the folder and every Mac shows the same grid.
SIP stays intact. No daemon, no kernel hack.

output.text: desktop created on the Studio display

stage.capText: double-click · fresh desktop · terminal in the folder · pane beside it

ritual.title: Eight steps, ten times a day.
ritual.lead: Every time you sit down with a project it is the same ritual. Times dozens of projects, every day, forever.
ritual.punch: loadcli does the eight. You do one.
steps: pick the model and the effort
spin up a desktop so you don't clutter the others

flow.title: What happens when you double-click.
flow.lead: Every window is verified. If one didn't land where it should, loadcli fixes it before handing control back to you.

cards.title: You double-click
cards.text: On the project's card. Or from the menu bar, without even opening the main window.

cards.title: The desktop is born
cards.text: A brand-new Space, on the monitor you chose. Your other desktops stay exactly as they were.

cards.title: The terminal opens ready
cards.text: Already in the project folder, running your CLI, on the model and effort that project asks for.

cards.title: Everything takes its place
cards.text: Browser at the deploy, a Finder folder, or just the terminal full screen. Focus ends where you are about to type.

card.title: The card lives inside the project folder.
card.lead: There is no project database. Each folder carries a LOADCLI.md, and that file is the card. loadcli walks the folders you registered, finds those documents, and builds the grid from what they say.
card.bodyText: The Acme store. Deployed on Vercel.

points.title: No absolute paths
points.text: The project folder is wherever the file sits. The same document works on any Mac, under any username.

points.title: Sync and you're done
points.text: Put your projects folder on Google Drive or ownCloud. Every Mac shows the same cards, always current.

points.title: The file is yours
points.text: Edit it in your editor, commit it to git. Keys you add and the markdown body survive every rewrite.

points.title: Opens instantly
points.text: The last scan is cached. The window paints right away and new cards appear a moment later.

ai.title: Every project with its own brain.
ai.lead: Claude Code in one, Codex in another, your own script in the third. Model and effort live in the project's file, so it opens exactly right. No flags to remember.

cards.title: Claude Code
cards.text: Model and effort per project. The command comes out assembled the way you configured it.

cards.title: Codex
cards.text: Same idea, with Codex's own flags. Change them at launch time if you feel like it.

cards.title: Custom command
cards.text: Anything that runs in a shell. loadcli does the cd and runs it.

ai.swatchLead: Every card with its own icon and colour. Ten seconds to glance across the grid and find the right project.

spaces.title: It creates desktops without you disabling SIP.
spaces.p1: Creating a Space through a private API does not work in a modern macOS app. That is why tiling tools ask you to turn System Integrity Protection off.
spaces.p2: loadcli does what a person would do: it drives Mission Control's + button through the Accessibility API, targets the monitor by its display id, and clicks the new desktop's thumbnail. Always verifying the result before moving on.
spaces.pull: SIP stays intact. No daemon. No kernel hack.

features.title: The rest of what you'll use every day.

items.title: Quick search
items.text: Type and the folders holding matches open themselves. Clear it and they all close again.

items.title: Recents
items.text: The projects you opened last, newest first.

items.title: Folders
items.text: Group by the document's group key. They start collapsed, so you can scan fast.

items.title: Multi-monitor
items.text: Pin the monitor per project, or let loadcli ask you every time.

items.title: Terminal font
items.text: It bumps the font up for you, as many times as you set.

items.title: Menu bar
items.text: Launch any project without opening the main window.

items.title: Self-test
items.text: loadcli --doctor checks the desktop mechanism on every monitor.

items.title: 100% native
items.text: SwiftUI, no Electron. Opens instantly and barely touches memory.

mac.name: loadcli 1.0.0
mac.meta: Apple Silicon · macOS 14 or newer · DMG
mac.noteText: the app has not been through Apple notarization yet. Right-click it and choose Open. If macOS still refuses, go to Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
